newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: IMF team agrees to resume standby loan to Pakistan.
newsitem.headline: IMF team agrees to resume standby loan to Pakistan.

text.p: An International Monetary Fund (IMF) team agreed after talks with Pakistani officials on Thursday to recommend that a stalled $600 million standby loan be reactivated and expanded, Pakistan's finance chief said.

Shahid Javed Burki, adviser on finance and economic affairs to caretaker Prime Minister Meraj Khalid, told a news conference that an IMF team led by its Middle East department director, Paul Chabrier, had confirmed a Letter of Intent drawn up with the fund by the ousted government of Benazir Bhutto last month.
He said the mission would recommend to the IMF board that it resume disbursements from the standby loan originally agreed with Pakistan in December 1995.

"It is expected that they will recommend larger assistance than was previously negotiated," he said. The IMF had withheld two tranches worth $80 million each, but Burki said he expected the IMF to make an extra up-front payment. He gave no figures.

Burki said he planned to go to Washington in early December to start talks with the IMF on an enhanced structural adjustment facility, saying he hoped an agreement on a new ESAF could be reached before the end of fiscal 1996/97 (July-June).
